Name: Unarmed Enhancer
Effects: A glove, gauntlet, handwraps, or other piece worn on the hand to aid in striking with the fists. This counts as an Unarmed weapon, and technically as a Held item, but does not occupy the slot. It has no specific benefit by itself, but can be enhanced as any other weapon, in which case it applies its benefits to the wielder’s Unarmed weapon attacks.

Name: Basic Clothing
Description (Fluff): Clothing includes items that might cover the Head, Neck, Hands, Torso, or Feet slots. This can be in any form, including cloaks, hats, gloves, boots, etc.
Effects: Clothing does not count as Armor of any kind.

Name: Basic Jewelry
Description (Fluff): Jewelry includes various items worn in the Head, Neck, Ring, Hands, and Feet slots. It can also include general, pretty jewelry that serves no purpose other than opulence and to demonstrate the wealth of the wearer.

Name: Adventurer's Kit
Description (Fluff): A general collection of useful items for any traveler. Nobody on the roads would be caught dead without one of these... or, rather, they very likely might.
Effects: Includes the following:Basic mess kit (utensils, metal bowl, etc.)Simple bedroll or blanketWaterskin (holds four liters)Utility knife20-meter coil of ropeTinderbox, with flint and steel

Name: Medicinal Supply
Description (Fluff): A bandage, salve, or other simple yet critical supply that aids in various types of first aid.
Effects: Medicinal supplies may be used in place of cards for certain Techniques.

Name: Basic Travel Ration
Description (Fluff): Hardtack, cured meat, dried fruits; through simple yet careful preparation, many kinds of food can be prepared for a long journey.
Effects: Per the rules, eating 1 Food item each day is required to avoid exhaustion. These rations are preserved and won’t spoil, so you can keep them until you need them.

Name: Knapsack
Description (Fluff): A small traveler's pack, worn across the back.
Effects: A container large enough to carry a few kits, toolsets, and some spare equipment.

Name: Backpack
Description (Fluff): A decent-sized bag with two sturdy straps and some small, outside pockets.
Effects: Can easily fit many kits and loose items, with room on the outside to strap one or two larger objects.Requires a Might Skill Total of 4 to carry.

Name: Rucksack
Description (Fluff): A large bag with multiple sections and pockets, almost resembling multiple smaller packs cobbled together. Due to its size and straps, it occupies your Belt slot.
Effects: Can fit several smaller containers, some spare armaments, and strap a few items to the outside.Requires a Might Skill Total of 6 to carry.

Name: Survivalist's Pack
Description (Fluff): A great pack, larger than a child, with multiple reinforced straps to allow it to be carried. Several hooks and loops on the outside allow almost an entire group's worth of armaments to be strapped to the outside. Due to its size and straps, it occupies your Belt slot.
Effects: Can fit almost a mule's worth of equipment, including practically anything the prepared traveler would require.Requires a Might Skill Total of 8 to carry.

Name: Adventurer's Belt
Description (Fluff): A sturdy belt with pouches for easy access to all manner of adventuring goods. It occupies your Belt slot.
Effects: The belt has 5 pouches, each of which is an easily-accessible container that can hold a small object such as a Potion, vial of Poison, or Grenade.

Name: Cart, Small
Description (Fluff): A small wooden cart, with long handles so that it can be pulled by a beast of burden.
Effects: Enough room to hold about a half-dozen barrels, 3-4 people, or a load of similar size.

Name: Musical Instrument
Description (Fluff): Lutes, trumpets, drums, and many more types of musical instruments are a common sight in civilized lands.

Name: Climber's Kit
Description (Fluff): A small leather pack, containing a variety of hooks, pitons, boot spikes, and other climbing gear all bundled tightly for easy transport. Contains everything you need to scale a wide variety of terrain without needing existing handholds.
Effects: This kit can reduce the penalty to climb difficult cliffs and walls, although some time might be needed for setup.

Name: Disguise Kit
Description (Fluff): A nondescript burlap bag cinched with hemp rope, this kit contains a basic assortment of materials to construct a disguise. Included are a small assortment of basic cosmetics for altering the appearance of your face as well as a variety of accessories for a number of disguises, including hats, bandannas, convincing but mostly worthless costume jewelry, and the like.
Effects: This kit allows you to put on a disguise for use with Masquerade. This kit only covers very general disguise requirements, such as basic makeup and common, simple clothing items. More specific or complex disguises might require additional costume pieces.

Name: Tinker's Kit
Description (Fluff): A small leather case strapped tightly, usually embossed with a small insignia of a guild or other organization, with a small buckle to keep it shut. Inside the case holds a variety of minute picks, screwdrivers, pins, and the like wrought from fine spring steel which allow for fine manipulation of locks and other mechanical devices.
Effects: These tools allow you to manipulate fine devices at no penalty, including picking locks, which might otherwise be difficult or outright impossible.

Name: Fisher's Kit
Effects: These tools allow you to fish in a variety of bodies of water at no penalty.

Name: Tailor's Kit
Description (Fluff): This is a set of standard tools required for crafting and repair work, usually a satchel containing hammers, chisels, nails, tongs, and the like. Specific tools might be required for very particular arts, but the bulk of projects can be finished with this set. It comes in a convenient leather case that rolls up tightly, and includes a small book of common references for working common materials.
Effects: This item fulfills the tool requirement for most items created with Tailoring. This also includes recipes for all level 1 Tailoring equipment and adventuring goods, with room to add more recipes.

Name: Carving Kit
Description (Fluff): This is a set of standard tools required for crafting and repair work, usually a satchel containing hammers, chisels, nails, tongs, and the like. Specific tools might be required for very particular arts, but the bulk of projects can be finished with this set. It comes in a convenient leather case that rolls up tightly, and includes a small book of common references for working common materials.
Effects: This item fulfills the tool requirement for most items created with Carving. This also includes recipes for all level 1 Carving equipment and adventuring goods, with room to add more recipes.

Name: Smithing Kit
Description (Fluff): This is a set of standard tools required for crafting and repair work, usually a satchel containing hammers, chisels, nails, tongs, and the like. Specific tools might be required for very particular arts, but the bulk of projects can be finished with this set. It comes in a convenient leather case that rolls up tightly, and includes a small book of common references for working common materials.
Effects: This item fulfills the tool requirement for most items created with Smithing, although a forge is usually still required. This also includes recipes for all level 1 Smithing equipment and adventuring goods, with room to add more recipes.

Name: Jeweler's Kit
Description (Fluff): This is a set of standard tools required for crafting and repair work, usually a satchel containing hammers, chisels, nails, tongs, and the like. Specific tools might be required for very particular arts, but the bulk of projects can be finished with this set. It comes in a convenient leather case that rolls up tightly, and includes a small book of common references for working common materials.
Effects: This item fulfills the tool requirement for most items created with Jewelrymaking. This also includes recipes for all level 1 Jewelrymaking equipment and adventuring goods, with room to add more recipes.

Name: Mixology Set
Description (Fluff): This is a set of beakers, spoons, vials, and measuring devices that no alchemist would be caught without, held safe in a small, sturdy box. Some projects might demand specific equipment, but with the handy charts and material listings kept in a waterproof folio this kit covers almost every need!
Effects: This item fulfills the tool requirement for most items created with Alchemy. This also includes recipes for all standard Alchemy-created alchemical goods, with room to add more recipes.

Name: Travel Rations
Description (Fluff): Hard tack, cured meat, dried fruits; through simple yet careful preparation, many kinds of food can be prepared for a long journey.
Effects: Travel rations are enough food for a single person for an entire day. They will never spoil, letting a skilled cook preserve Food ingredients indefinitely.

Name: Power Snack
Description (Fluff): A quick yet tasty meal to help you take on the day!
Effects: This is a full day's meal. In addition, you may Sift [six times Level] cards.

Name: Hearty Meal
Description (Fluff): A delicious, filling meal augmented by nutritious herbs, hearty broth, or just a lot of extra food.
Effects: This is a full day's meal. In addition, the next time you get a full night's rest, you heal an extra [Level] Shallow Health.

Name: Muscular Feast
Description (Fluff): A dense dish packed with powerful foods, filling you with energy and vitality.
Effects: This is a full day's meal. In addition, until you get a full night's rest, the next [twice Level] times you would gain a stack of Bleeding, Crippled, or Slowed, instead you don't. If you would gain multiple effects at the same time, but this effect wouldn't prevent all of them, you may choose which stacks to prevent.

Name: Soul Soup
Description (Fluff): A relaxing meal with balanced flavors and vitamins, bringing a feeling of harmony and clarity.
Effects: This is a full day's meal. In addition, you gain [Level] Nutrition points that last until you get a full night's rest. When you use an Encounter Technique, you may pay [that Technique’s Level] Nutrition points. If you do, you don’t expend a use of it.

Name: Acidic Flask
Description (Fluff): Originally regarded as a useless byproduct of a botched process, potential was seen and after much refinement a method for creating strong acid was born. An Acidic Flask is composed of a caustic mixture that clings to whatever surface it is shattered against, burning and warping flesh.
Effects: On a hit, the target gains 5 + [Clubs] stacks of Bleeding.

Name: Immaculate Adhesive
Description (Fluff): The most refined and effective formula for glue, these adhesives are used in many crafts: bookbinding, armorworking, carpentry, tile-laying, and many more possibilities. Only a small amount of adhesive is needed to bind two materials, and excessive use of glue causes the material to rebound off of itself, with a high risk of splattering.
Effects: Each dose of adhesive can cover a surface up to 3 meters in radius, hardening after 1 minute. Any items placed on the glue during this time and left there will become adhered to the surface, requiring enough force to remove that it would damage both objects in the process.When thrown as a Grenade, instead of making an attack as usual, choose a space within the weapon's Range. That space and all spaces adjacent to it each gain 2 levels of Difficult Terrain that last for the encounter.

Name: Bottled Fire
Description (Fluff): A staple of any resourceful adventurer, a glass flask of Bottled Fire contains a mix of reagents that react violently when smashed on a surface, engulfing the point of impact in an intense plume of flame. The concoction results in a quick flash of particularly hot fire, and as such will ignite most flammable materials it strikes.
Effects: On a hit it deals 8 Fire damage.

Name: Smokejar
Description (Fluff): A smokejar consists of a stone or clay flask containing a small glass bubble, both of which contain alchemical reagents. When the glass bubble inside is shattered and the materials react with each other - usually accomplished by either shattering the jar on the ground or shaking it violently - a great amount of smoke billows out of the mixture, obscuring vision.
Effects: When thrown or broken, the jar creates a cloud of smoke in a 1-meter-radius circle centered on the jar. At the start of your next 2 turns the radius increases by 1, eventually covering a 3-meter-radius area. The smoke hangs in the air for the scene or until dispersed by a strong wind. The smoke acts as Heavy Cover in its area.The jar can also be thrown as a Grenade. If the attack hits, the target is Crippled 3 + [Clubs] times. Then, the smoke cloud is created in the target's space if the attack hits or is Parried, otherwise it is created in the space behind them.

Name: Bonemelter
Description (Fluff): An horrifying mixture of uncommon reagents, frequently employing byproducts harvested from demonic entities, once prepared this grenade explodes into a toxic mist that wreaks bodily havoc on the victim.
Effects: On a hit, before damage or any other effects the target gains 3 + [Diamonds] stacks of Necrotic, then it deals 8 Shadow damage.

Name: Snowstorm
Description (Fluff): A glass flask of Snowstorm contains a mix of reagents that react instantly when smashed on a surface and quickly leech heat from anything the chemicals touch as part of the reaction. The concoction results in a quick-acting mixture that dramatically chills anything it spreads across before evaporating, including most liquids if they are not in a sufficiently insulated container.
Effects: On a hit it deals 8 Frost damage and the target is Slowed 3 + [Spades] times.

Name: Sunbeam
Description (Fluff): A stabilized mixture of spiritually-energized materials that erupts suddenly when sufficiently disturbed.
Effects: On a hit it deals 9 Brilliant damage and the target gains 4 + [Diamonds] stacks of Vulnerable.

Name: Hellfire Bomb
Description (Fluff): By combining extremely volatile reagents and suspending them in a total vacuum, a talented alchemist can create a veritable inferno in a nutshell.
Effects: Make an attack against all creatures adjacent to the target. On a hit it deals 8 Fire damage.

Name: Thunderclap-in-a-Jar
Description (Fluff): Originally a modification of the common Bottled Fire, after much work the recipe found enough distinction to be regarded as its own grenade, named the Thunderclap (in a jar) for the intense concussive blast that is produced when the container is shattered and the reagents mix. Rather than scorching its victims, the sheer force and metal fragments in the jar cause the bulk of the destruction.
Effects: Instead of attacking a target, choose a space within range of the Grenade. Make an attack against all creatures in or adjacent to the space. On a hit it deals 8 Physical damage, and the target gains 2 + [Diamonds] stacks of Harried and 2 + [Clubs] stacks of Bleeding.

Name: Energizing Brew
Description (Fluff): Many civilizations have plants native to their climate which can be roasted, dried, pulverized, and otherwise prepared for making some manner of drink out of. These brews all have in common that they increase the drinker's attention, perception, and wakefulness, as well as being a cornerstone of many fast-breaking rituals.
Effects: When consumed, until you take a full night's rest you have Good Luck on Reflex flips.

Name: Fortifying Concoction
Description (Fluff): Frequently stocked in the supplies of anyone who might anticipate a fight, from mercenary companies to lone woodsmen, this ages-old recipe bolsters the body with a burst of energy and helps reduce any bruising or swelling.
Effects: When consumed, you gain 3 stacks of Protected.

Name: Elemental-Attuned Tincture
Description (Fluff): This mixture creates a negative elemental current in the body of the imbiber which helps ground them and render them somewhat immune to harmful magic and other manifestations of a certain element.
Effects: When this Potion is created, choose Fire, Frost, Brilliant, or Shadow. When consumed, you gain 3 stacks of [chosen type] Ward. Unlike normal Fleeting effects, these stacks don't decay from time passing during combat — instead, 1 stack is removed every hour.
Main Materials: The opposite of the chosen element - Fire for Frost, Brilliant for Shadow, and vice versa

Name: Essential Ointment
Description (Fluff): Made as tiny jars filled with energized salves, vials of oils to be splashed on the face, and herbal pastes that are applied to the energetic centers of the body. Regardless of how it is constructed, these are designed to be quickly and easily applied to the user, causing their body to quickly metabolize energy from their surroundings.
Effects: When consumed, you draw 2 cards.

Name: Soldier's Salts
Description (Fluff): These take a variety of different forms, known to be made as small pieces of rune-etched ceramic, tiny jars filled with energized salves, and vials of ointment to be splashed on the face. Regardless of how it is constructed, these are designed to be quickly and easily applied to the user and provide a quick burst of invigoration.
Effects: When consumed, you regain the use of any Encounter Technique level 2 or lower.

Name: Calming Brew
Effects: When consumed, ignore the next 4 total stacks of Taunted and/or Frightened you would gain until you take a full night's rest. If you already have stacks of either, remove them and count them against the total.

Name: Healing Potion
Description (Fluff): A staple of any true adventurer, healing potions contain a mix of specially prepared medicines that help the body resist trauma and shock and aid in blood clotting and other functions that are pretty useful to someone who has been stabbed.
Effects: When consumed, you heal 2 Health.

Name: Liquid Charisma
Effects: When consumed, for 1 hour you have Good Luck on all Presence, Persuasion, and Rapport flips.

Name: Earthen Draught
Description (Fluff): Distilling powerful concoctions related to the earth - medicinal bark from old trees, blood of strong predators - produces a syrupy elixir that reinforces one's vitality and strengthens their body against assault.
Effects: When consumed, for 1 hour, at the end of each of your turns, you gain enough stacks of Protected so that you have 2 stacks (before any other effects apply).

Name: Fighter's Friend
Description (Fluff): An extremely refined version of the popular Soldier's Salts, requiring rare and powerful materials to produce. Reserved for only the greatest of fighters.
Effects: When consumed, you regain the use of any Encounter Technique level 3 or lower.

Name: Battlemaster's Brew
Description (Fluff): A closely-guarded recipe passed between the training halls of true battlemasters, this thick, bitter brew is said to steady the hand and clear the mind at the exact moment a fight demands everything you have left to give. Vanishingly few alchemists know how to make it properly.
Effects: When consumed, you regain the use of any Encounter Technique level 4 or lower.

Name: Swiftblade Vial
Effects: When consumed, you are Hasted eight times, and you may adjust your position in turn order by up to 3.

Name: Insanity Potion
Description (Fluff): While not the most descriptive name for a potion, it is nonetheless fitting as one may very well have to be mentally disturbed to consider voluntarily drinking it. That being said, the benefits of the Insanity Potion are to be considered, for while it does wreak havoc on a person's physical well-being it also bolsters their strength tremendously, and provided you have medical care for the after-effects it is usually survivable.
Effects: When consumed, for 1 hour you gain the following: A +1 bonus to Speed. Ignore any penalties for being Wounded, Crippled, or Slowed. If your attack hits or is Parried, the target gains a stack of Bleeding. You cannot heal any Health or gain any stacks of Protected.

Name: Basic Poison
Description (Fluff): A broad category encompassing a variety of lethal and particularly toxic poisons, which are quasi-legal at most but still popular among less scrupulous folk. A staggering number of sources can be "refined" to make poisons; cheaper doses simply use substances that are incompatible with the body such as oil, animal venom, and hazardous waste from magical experiments. More refined assassins, however, have even been known to summon minor demons just to render their blood into a pure poison of corruption. No matter what, one rule holds: don’t drink it.
Effects: Choose a Basic Poison; you make a dose of that poison with a Concentration of [3 + Level] and a Potency of [Level].

Name: Crippling Poison
Description (Fluff): Rather than trying to kill the target outright, this poison is designed to cause wracking pains and muscle spasms that hinder the victim's movements.
Effects: An affected creature suffers [Potency] stacks of Crippled.

Name: Bloody Poison
Description (Fluff): A basic but very commonly used substance, designed to simply cause the victim as much harm as possible.
Effects: A target affected by this poison gains [twice its Potency] stacks of Bleeding. If the target ingested the poison, they instead gain [four times its Potency] stacks of Bleeding. Unlike other Poisons, these stacks expire normally.

Name: Slowing Poison
Description (Fluff): Frequently used by lawmen and bounty hunters, this poison saps the energy from the victim's limbs and makes their breath heavy in their lungs.
Effects: An affected creature suffers [Potency] stacks of Slowed.

Name: Necrotic Poison
Description (Fluff): A particularly unsavory poison, as soon as it enters the victim's bloodstream they find their wounds almost impossible to close.
Effects: A target affected by this poison suffers [three times its Potency] stacks of Necrotic. These stacks can still be removed through Necrotic's other usual rules.

Name: Vulnerability Poison
Description (Fluff): Wracking the body with fever-like symptoms and clouding the mind similarly, this niche poison is used to render the victim susceptible to further poisons as well as dark hexes and other magicks.
Effects: An affected creature suffers [twice its Potency] stacks of Vulnerable.

Name: Harrying Poison
Description (Fluff): Favored by kidnappers and mercenaries who need to bring their targets in alive, this poison saps the strength from its victim and removes their ability to defend themselves.
Effects: An affected creature suffers [twice its Potency] stacks of Harried.

Name: Psychosis Poison
Effects: An affected creature suffers [twice its Potency] stacks of the following effect:As long as you have any stacks of this, if you are hit by a damaging attack then you are Frightened of the attacker once.

Name: Cowl of Tranquility
Description (Fluff): A loose hood stitched from prayer shawls and adorned with simple beads, when donned the wearer feels faint, insubstantial energy flowing through them, like a flowing river or a spring breeze.
Effects: This item starts each encounter with [Level] charges. When you would gain a stack of Taunted or Frightened, you may expend a charge from this and instead you don’t gain that stack.

Name: Mask of Night
Description (Fluff): Anything from a hardened leather mask to a black hood attached to a bandana, the headpiece serves to grant improved vision at night as well as conceal the face; a likely consequence of its original development, as far as anyone can tell, among thieves and rogues.
Effects: When the mask is in place it grants its wearer perfect vision in darkness, negating any penalty to sight due to a lack of light. Smoke or anything else that physically obscures sight is not negated, however.

Name: Lens of Daybreak
Description (Fluff): Appearing either as a monocle, glasses, or any variety of single- or double-lensed accessories, these lenses have frames made from precious metals and usually have fine inscription work along them. These lenses help the wearer's eyes pierce fog, chase away darkness, dampen excessively-bright light, and so on, making it much easier to see through any difficult circumstances.
Effects: The wearer has Good Luck on Awareness flips that specifically involve sight.

Name: Confident Cap
Description (Fluff): These hats are simple but impressively crafted, designed in an understated fashion but woven with silver threading and other fine materials. The styling of the hats varies, and with that the effects seem to as well - some are styled in a stylish manner that gives the wearer a boost of smugness, and others with clashing, distracting motifs that help them regain their footing in a conversation. Regardless, every expert negotiator can be seen sporting such a hat.
Effects: This starts each encounter with 5 charges. Whenever you are in the front in a social contest and your party would gain a Concession, instead you may expend a charge and you don’t gain that Concession.

Name: Crown of Glory
Description (Fluff): A glorious crown of precious metals, striking enough to inspire respect from anyone. Such impressive regalia naturally calms and inspires both the wearer and their allies, driving them forward to victory.
Effects: Once per day, for 0 AP, the wearer may have themselves and up to 4 allies who can see them each draw a card.

Name: Choker of Silent Whispers
Description (Fluff): A tight-fitting necklace, woven with fine silver chains and clear crystals typically used in divination magics. With concentration, it carries the wearer's whispers a great distance, to a specific someone.
Effects: The wearer can mutter inaudibly (nobody else can actually hear that you're talking) while focusing on a specific person within 10 meters, carrying a clear message only to that person. They hear the message as though the wearer were speaking clearly at a normal volume, in the wearer's voice, and will be able to tell that the wearer is sending the message if they see the wearer whispering.

Name: Cloak of Caches
Description (Fluff): A favorite of travelers, this large cloak is made from warm quilted fabric and furs, featuring a charming buckle of silver, gold, or similar metal. Inside the cloak are a set of large, useful pockets that seem to hold many useful trinkets.
Effects: As though using an easily-accessible location, the wearer may reach into the cloak and pull out any of the following:a set of metal utensilsa metal bowla simple yet warm blanketa small utility knifea 20-meter coil of ropea flint and steel seta small glass jara spool of twine (roughly 10 meters' worth)a wooden "coin"a pair of crude bone diceOnly one of each item can be produced at a time. At the end of the encounter, any produced items or their remains fade away as though someone set them down and forgot where they put them, unless you specifically wish otherwise for a given item.

Name: Diver's Necklace
Description (Fluff): Fashioned as a string of pearls, driftwood, and riverstones, these necklaces are not ostentatious but behind their plain appearance lies a useful enchantment. While fastened around their neck, the wearer finds that water passes into their lungs as easily as air, and benefits their body just the same.
Effects: The wearer can breathe in water perfectly as though it were air.

Name: Snowfall Drape
Description (Fluff): A large, soft, warm cloak made to keep the wearer warm in the harshest of snowstorms. A mystical power of this cloak allows the wearer to leave a trail of thick, fluffy snow in their wake, leading some to believe it actually absorbs chill from around it, storing it for later use.
Effects: Once per encounter, when you move, you may ruffle the cloak and leave snow in the first 3 spaces you move from that action. Those spaces each gain [Level] degrees of Difficult Terrain that last for the encounter.

Name: Elemental-Resistant Armor
Description (Fluff): A very broad category for a common enchantment (as common as magic items might be, anyway), armor can be enchanted to resist a variety of elemental types. Mundane armor provides only Physical Soak - no protection against Fire damage, for example - but armor might be enchanted to protect the wearer against Fire, Frost, Shadow, or (rarely) Brilliant damage.
Effects: The wearer gains a +1 bonus to Fire, Frost, Brilliant, or Shadow Resist, chosen when the item is created. If the enhancement is Level 2, it increases to a total of +2 Resist of the chosen type.
Main Materials: The opposite of the chosen element - Fire for Frost, Brilliant for Shadow, and vice versa

Name: Dauntless Wrap
Description (Fluff): Clothing or armor created with thick threading, firm metal wire, and many other sturdy materials. While worn it imparts a sense of security and snugness, and is prized for its supernatural ability to keep someone in the fight even when their strength would otherwise fail.
Effects: The first time each day that losing Health would Down you, before you lose that Health you gain [thrice the enhancement's Level] stacks of Protected.

Name: Armor of Constitutional Integrity
Description (Fluff): Applicable to both armor as well as formal dress, garments with this enhancement stabilize the wearer’s vital energy as well as protecting it from all manner of toxin. They are worn frequently by a variety of people, from those who live a life of adventure to nobility who often fear for threats of assassination.
Effects: Any attack against the wearer by a Poison, Disease, or similar bodily threat has Bad Luck. The wearer also has Good Luck on Resilience flips.

Name: Coat of Knit Flesh
Description (Fluff): This suit of armor includes woven leathers, dyed deep reds and purples. While donned the wearer feels a sense of calm, relaxed energy and over time will rarely find themselves with minor scrapes and bruises, even after a deal of physical labor.
Effects: Each day, the first 2 (if Level 2) or 4 (if Level 4) stacks of Bleeding the wearer would gain are ignored instead.

Name: Fortified Armor
Description (Fluff): Immaculately-crafted armor with an inlay of hardened beast scales, the enhancement placed on such a suit of armor further reinforces its defensive ability and narrowly deflects blows that would otherwise strike at vital points.
Effects: If the wearer is hit by an attack for which a red card was flipped, and this armor has a Resist against that type of damage, increase the Resist by 1 against that attack.

Name: Lifeforce Plate
Description (Fluff): Regardless of construction, this garment is reinforced with plates and rods of polished bone, bolstering the vitality of the wearer and allowing them to shrug off minor injuries.
Effects: At the end of the wearer's turn, if the wearer has no stacks of Protected they gain 1 stack. Then, if the enhancement is Level 5, and the wearer has fewer than 2 stacks of Protected, they gain an additional stack.

Name: Robes of Resilience
Description (Fluff): These robes are often stitched together from patches of various materials, however even under heavy use the robes remain intact and unworn. Rather than provide their own protection against attacks the enchantment on them fortifies the wearer's body to resist assault.
Effects: These robes grant a +1 bonus to Physical, Fire, Frost, Shadow, and Brilliant Resist.
Main Materials: Metal, Bone, Fire, Frost, Shadow, Brilliant

Name: Robes of the Elemental Lord
Description (Fluff): An immensely powerful enchantment, originally pioneered by an extraordinary warmage renowned for his elemental magics, these garments have only been replicated by the best enchanters available and at great cost. An unparalleled defense against other elementalists, these robes grant no protection against swords and arrows but insulate the wearer from blizzards and firestorms with ease.
Effects: These robes grant a +3 bonus to Fire, Frost, Brilliant, and Shadow Resists.

Name: Armory Gauntlets
Description (Fluff): Thick, unadorned iron gloves which are designed either for austerity or inconspicuousness depending on who is asked. Their simple appearance conceals a substantial utility, as the wearer of the Armory Gauntlets is never truly unarmed or defenseless.
Effects: For 0 AP the wielder can conjure a weapon made of shimmering force which appears in their hand. This can be any single weapon, including shields and the like. Only one weapon may be conjured at a time, although if the wielder has conjured a ranged weapon they may also conjure ammunition for it as part of an attack without counting against this limit. The wielder may dismiss any conjured weapon at any time.

Name: Deft Gloves
Description (Fluff): Fingerless gloves made out of a thin, black leather and secured with small buckles, these manage to support and steady the wearer's hands while their magic helps them move carefully and gracefully.
Effects: The wearer of these gloves has Good Luck on Craft flips for working with small devices, such as locks and other mechanisms. These gloves also count as though they were tinker's tools, and the wearer does not need any extra equipment to work with small devices without penalty.

Name: Mighty Mitts
Effects: Your hands (the ones wearing these) are as effective at destroying things, causing you to ignore any penalties to Might flips to break things without having a proper tool for smashing, prying, and so on. You also have Good Luck on Might flips to move or destroy things.Once per day, the mitts can grant you a burst of strength. This takes 4AP to use, and allows you to make flips to move or destroy something as though you had spent a minute doing so.

Name: Flamebinder's Promise
Description (Fluff): A ring of dull brass etched with black marks, embedded with burnt-colored jewels. These versatile and useful trinkets can only be created by a jeweler with a strong connection to the element of fire, and grant the wearer a measure of control over it.
Effects: Once per encounter, for 2 AP, the wearer may throw a ball of fire at a nearby creature. This is an Acrobatics attack against the Dodge Defense of a target within 5 meters, dealing 3 + [Mind] Fire damage.

Name: Focusing Band of [Technique]
Description (Fluff): Coveted for their usefulness and rarity, these rings hold the skill and knowledge of their crafter. Through careful meditation and focus, the jeweler binds their ability into a small token that can be tapped into when worn, allowing another person - who might be entirely unfamiliar with the art - to replicate it.
Effects: When this ring is created, the creator chooses a Technique they know, which must be the same Level as this ring.The wearer may discard a card at any time in order to “learn” the chosen Technique until they get a full night’s rest or take the ring off. During this time they are treated as though they know the Technique, or an extra copy of it if it’s an Encounter or Duplicate Technique.

Name: Tactician's Band
Description (Fluff): An austere, silver ring, etched with markings from battlemaps, warmage tomes, or other works that prominently feature tactical maneuvers and other strategies. The ring helps focus the wearer's thoughts, keeping their tactics one step ahead of any opponent.
Effects: This starts each day (after you get a full night’s rest) with [five times Level] charges. At any time, you may expend a charge, discard a card from your hand, and draw a card.

Name: Bloodshard Ring
Description (Fluff): A band made of twisted wire holding shards of bone and deep red gemstones. It is as favored by warmages and other arcanists who find themselves in combat situations as it is frowned upon by more academic, bookish sorts.
Effects: Before making a spell attack that deals damage, the wearer may spend X Health. If they do, the spell attack deals its damage as Fire, and deals an extra X damage. If the spell attack only has one target, then instead it deals an extra [twice X] damage.

Name: Fate’s Grasp
Effects: Whenever you discard or play cards from your hand, after that effect is resolved, you may Sift up to that many cards.

Name: Galeforce Loop
Description (Fluff): A winding ring of finely-carved wood, seeming wrapping a dozen times around the wearer's finger. The wearer seems to feel the breeze more strongly on their hand, and can cause the wind to suddenly swell at their command.
Effects: Once per encounter, the wearer may cause a strong gust of wind around themself. This gust does not blow in any particular direction, but blows around the area strongly enough to snuff out torches, scatter paper, disperse clouds of smoke, and so on. Though the effect is dramatic, there is no indication that the wearer is responsible for the wind.

Name: Heartbinding Band
Description (Fluff): A band of dull metal with soft, pink gemstones embedded in it which seem to pulse with a faint light.
Effects: The wearer may spend 1 AP, place their hand (the one with the ring) on an adjacent willing creature, and spend any amount of Health. That creature then heals that much Health.

Name: Poison Needle
Description (Fluff): A large ring of iron, covering an entire finger joint, and relatively unassuming at first glance. Hidden mechanisms allow the ring to store a dose of poison, which can be quickly applied to a weapon.
Effects: The wearer can spend a full minute to place a dose of poison inside the ring, where it can remain indefinitely. When the wearer declares an attack with a weapon, as an Interrupt for 0 AP they may apply the poison in the ring to that weapon.

Name: Flamefist's Approach
Description (Fluff): A deceptively simple ring that, upon further inspection, is finely-crafted gold and silver inlaid with rubies. The ring seems to attune the wearer's energies with ambient elemental energies, melding their martial arts and their war magics.
Effects: The ring has two powers:If you hit a creature with a Brawl attack, you may cast a Sorcery Spell Technique as long as it targets at least one target of your Brawl attack and takes no more than 2 AP to use.If you hit a creature with a Sorcery Spell attack and that creature is within [Meditation Skill Total] meters, you may Teleport into a space adjacent to the creature.You may use each of these powers once per encounter. Additionally, you may discard a card to use either power regardless of the ring’s limit.

Name: Luminous Signet
Description (Fluff): A large golden ring, encrusted with jewels, fit for a leader, hero, or other inspiring figure.
Effects: Whenever you discard or play cards from your hand, all allies within 5 meters of you are each Hasted [cards discarded/played] times.

Name: Assassin's Undetectable Arms
Description (Fluff): Tending towards the slender and unremarkable, these weapons have shadow worked into them and are crafted to avoid notice and search.
Effects: Regardless of its type or construction, some feature or enhancement of the weapon allows it to be concealed on your person. Furthermore, you have Good Luck on any flip to keep it hidden, and anyone attempting to search you for it or detect it has Bad Luck on the associated flip.

Name: Bounty Hunter's Blade
Description (Fluff): Traditionally crafted as blunt weapons, contrary to the name, these arms are designed to focus the force and energy of their blows across a wide area. As a result, they are largely unable to deal lethal blows to enemies, instead exhausting them and beating them into submission.
Effects: Non-lethal attacks with this don't have Bad Luck.

Name: Battering Armament
Description (Fluff): Thick and heavy, with ram motifs etched along many surfaces. Weapons crafted in this style are heavier than they appear - which is rather heavy - and difficult to block or knock aside.
Effects: When an attack with this weapon hits or is Parried, the target is Pushed 1 meter in a direction of your choice.

Name: Eager Armament
Description (Fluff): An uncommon style of weapon, although very favored by travelers and those who prefer to appear unarmed. Designed so that, no matter where one keeps it, the weapon is easy to grab.
Effects: Drawing the weapon from any location within reach only takes 0 AP.

Name: Fatestealer
Description (Fluff): Grim motifs decorate this weapon that, through magic or craftsmanship, somehow guides its wielder to become more deft as the battle rages on. A series of runes run along the blade, head, or other prominent part of the weapon, glowing with increasing intensity the more the wielder battles.
Effects: When an attack with this weapon Downs a creature, that creature is instantly killed and the weapon gains up to [enhancement's Level] charges.The weapon may not have more than 5 charges at any time, and when the wielder gets a full night’s rest all charges are lost.At any time, the wielder may spend charges on the following:For 1 charge, the wielder may Sift 2 cardsFor 3 charges, the wielder may draw a card

Name: Reaching Weapon
Description (Fluff): Master smiths can craft weapons that are reinforced or otherwise constructed to feature an unparalleled length without breaking or proving too unwieldy. Sometimes this is a matter of superior craftsmanship, sometimes it is due to specialized materials or imbuing the weapon with magic, but no matter the method the weapons defy normal conventions of combat to strike far beyond normal reach.
Effects: Attacks made with this weapon have their Range increased by [this power's Level], as do abilities used with it.For abilities that are not ranged normally, the wielder may choose any point within [this power's Level] meters of themself to be their location for the purposes of determining the ability's targets or area of effect.

Name: Venomous Weapon
Description (Fluff): A favorite of assassins and cunning killers of all stripes, these weapons are as dangerous as they are prized. Crafted with grooves along the blade or other striking surface of the weapon to allow poison to quickly streak down the weapon, or onto ammunition if the weapon is a bow or similar armament.
Effects: When created, a Basic Poison is chosen, with a Concentration of +[3 + X] and a Potency of X, where X is the enhancement’s Level. The first time each encounter that a weapon attack or ability using this as an Implement causes a target to lose Health or gain stacks of Bleeding, they expose it to this poison.

Name: Grim Promise
Description (Fluff): Adorned with bone and faint inscriptions, traditionally these weapons were carried by certain tribal warriors into battles they believed they would not survive. Why carry them, then? To make sure their enemies died first.
Effects: When attacking or parrying with this weapon, the wielder ignores any penalties from being Wounded or Crippled.

Name: Sorcerer's Bow
Description (Fluff): This bow is extremely durable despite seeming thin and fragile, with a strange construction that lacks any kind of bow string. When the wielder concentrates and channels magical energy, gemstones along the bow trace a glittering pattern as a string of pure light is created, allowing the wielder to shoot arrows of magical force from it.
Effects: This weapon uses Sorcery as its relevant Skill, deals damage based on the wielder’s Mind instead of Cunning, and has a Might Skill Total requirement of 3.

Name: Weapon of Sending
Description (Fluff): A bizarre enhancement in which a weapon is created in such a manner that it can be thrown with moderate accuracy, then returns to the wielder.
Effects: This weapon can be thrown as an Acrobatics attack, with Range 3 × [Body]. When the weapon is thrown as part of an attack, at the start of your next turn the weapon returns to your hand.

Name: Claw of Mortality
Description (Fluff): Usually crafted as daggers and ritual knives, or occasionally other edged weapons that employ black, glassy stone and similar natural materials. Creating an imbalance of spiritual energies, magic channeled through the claw tears away at the victim's life force.
Effects: When an attack with this weapon hits, before any damage or other effects are applied, the target gains 2 stacks of Necrotic. Non-weapon attacks made through this deal their damage as Shadow.

Name: Claw of Rime
Effects: When an attack with this weapon hits, before any damage or other effects are applied, the target is Slowed once. Non-weapon attacks made through this deal their damage as Frost.

Name: Conflagration Brand
Description (Fluff): A staff of charred wood or blade of blackened metal, twisting magical energy into pure, explosive, elemental force. Attacks from this cruel weapon blister and crack where they strike, causing even greater damage to their victims.
Effects: When an attack with this weapon hits, before any damage or other effects are applied, the target gains a stack of Bleeding. Non-weapon attacks made through this deal their damage as Fire.

Name: Elemental-Forged Weaponry
Description (Fluff): Often etched with runes of power or augmented with some material to make them more magically conductive, these weapons convert part of each attack made with them into the enchantment's corresponding element. These weapons usually give distinct visual cues that their enchantments are in effect, as a flaming sword might have gouts of flame leap off the blade with each attack and a shadowed axe might have the blade wreathed in darkness.
Effects: When the weapon is made, Fire is chosen; if the enhancement is Level 4, Frost, Brilliant, or Shadow may be chosen instead.Attacks with this weapon deal their damage as that type, instead of their usual type.

Name: Fanged Guard
Description (Fluff): Weapons and shields designed for parrying and blocking, frequently styled with spikes, thorns, barbs.
Effects: When the weapon is used to successfully Parry an attack from an adjacent creature, that creature gains a stack of Bleeding.

Name: Thrumming Focus
Description (Fluff): A weapon gently trembling with power; by focusing, the wielder can draw this power out and use it to strike true.
Effects: The wielder may spend an extra 1 AP for any action involving an attack with this weapon. If they do, any such attack has Good Luck.

Name: Apocalyptic Staff
Description (Fluff): Etched with a series of runes, appearing crude to the untrained eye but done in a manner to tap into chaotic energies and direct them in wild and unpredictable ways.
Effects: Once per encounter, the wielder may choose a version of the Elementalist's Artillery (Level 4) battle magic Technique, selecting any features as though they were learning the Spell, and cast it as though they knew it.

Name: Sash of Deep Pockets
Description (Fluff): A subtle and minimal-looking sash, concealing a dozen small pockets in its folds. Surprisingly, these pockets can hold much larger objects than a belt pouch normally would.
Effects: Each of the sash’s 12 pouches can hold one object at a time, and as long as an object is no larger than 1 meter in any dimension it can be stored in a pouch, distorting as it slips away into the small opening. Items are stored and retrieved from pouches as though it were an easily-accessible location. While stored items are weightless and cannot be damaged, and if the sash is destroyed the items tumble out of it, unharmed.

Name: Smuggler’s Belt
Description (Fluff): A worn, simple, common-looking belt.
Effects: The belt has 5 visible pouches, each of which is an easily-accessible container that can hold a small object such as a Potion, vial of Poison, or Grenade.The secret of the belt is that each pouch actually has two separate compartments within the belt, only one of which can be seen at a time. The wearer may manipulate the belt to determine which compartment is visible, which is a completely Subtle action that no onlookers will notice. Anyone who is not familiar with the specific belt will automatically fail any attempt to discover the non-visible compartments.

Name: Cobblestone Boots
Description (Fluff): A thick, sturdy pair of boots with soles and heels made entirely of rough-hewn rock, although they are surprisingly comfortable and easy to wear in all terrains. When the wearer wades into a body of water, however, their legs move with no resistance from the water.
Effects: The wearer may move with no penalty underwater, at their full Speed, but the wearer is unaffected by any sort of buoyancy and walks along the floor of whatever body of water, moving simply as though the water were not there. Any other complications of being underwater, such as penalties to using weapons underwater or being unable to breathe underwater, are not mitigated by these boots and affect the wearer normally.

Name: Feathered Sandals
Description (Fluff): A breathtaking number of soft, smooth feathers (or materials patterned as such) are stitched into the sides of these soft sandals. The wearer feels a subtle lightness from their feet, as though they could jump from a balcony and float to the ground like a piece of parchment.
Effects: The wearer automatically succeeds on flips to avoid damage when falling 10 meters or less, suffering no damage or other penalty.

Name: Lightfoot Shoes
Description (Fluff): Ubiquitous across all peoples who weave magical power into items, these shoes come in virtually all shapes, sizes, designs, and materials. As such identifying these shoes at a glance is nearly impossible, although any exceptional footwear stand a good chance of having this enchantment.
Effects: These footwear give a +[enhancement's Level] bonus to Speed while worn.

Name: Slipstream Sandals
Description (Fluff): Lightweight shoes woven with threads of silver and etched with runes that reach out to nearby magical currents, the subtle enchantment is nonetheless very useful and valued by experienced adventurers.
Effects: Once per encounter, for 0 AP, the boots allow the wearer to Teleport 3 meters.

Name: Vaulting Boots
Description (Fluff): Usually crafted as a light pair of leather boots with supple soles, these boots are widely used by all manner of adventurous individuals for their simple yet useful enchantment.
Effects: Once per encounter you may spend 1 AP to make a jump, without requiring a running start or a flip, up to 10 meters in any direction, and if you fall as part of the jump you ignore up to 10 meters of distance for the purpose of determining the difficulty of the Acrobatics flip to avoid falling damage.

Name: Greaves of the Stalwart Guardian
Description (Fluff): Appearing to be crude iron boots, heavy and awkward, the greaves feel as light as sandals and don’t encumber the wearer at all. Rather, when worn, they impart an unshakable sense of stability and steadfastness.
Effects: You cannot be unwillingly knocked over, Pushed, Shifted, Teleported, or otherwise moved unless they wish to be. Additionally, you ignore up to 3 degrees of Difficult Terrain at all times.This item starts each encounter with 5 charges. When you would gain a stack of Slowed, you may expend a charge from this and instead you don’t gain that stack.

Name: Evertoking Bottle
Description (Fluff): A detailed metal carafe topped by a jeweled cap, fastened to the bottle by a fine chain. Through glass or jewels on the bottle one can occasionally see a faint haze moving within, as though smoke billowed about inside the bottle. When the cap is removed the bottle produces an endless supply of faintly herbal smoke, as a hookah or other water pipe that is being actively stoked.
Effects: For 1 AP the holder can remove the cap and cause the bottle to produce a cloud of smoke in a 2-meter-radius circle centered on the holder. This smoke provides Light Cover to anything in its area, or for the targets of any attacks made by someone in the area. The smoke hangs in the air for the encounter or until dispersed by a strong wind. The bottle can only produce one cloud per encounter.If a creature that ends their turn in the cloud, make an attack with a bonus of +6 against their Vital Defense. If it hits, they gain the following based on the suit of the card flipped for the attack:Spade: 2 stacks of NecroticClub: 1 stack of VulnerableDiamond: 1 stack of SlowedHearts: 1 stack of Crippled

Name: Distant Scroll Cases
Description (Fluff): A finely-made cylindrical case of horn, wood, or the like and immaculately engraved with a series of runes and glyphs, these cases usually come with a sturdy carrying strap and a lid that clasps firmly onto the opening of the case. Inside the case has room for a large sheaf of papers to be rolled and secured.
Effects: These cases are always produced in identical pairs, and have the wondrous property that they share the space inside of them, allowing documents or small objects placed in one case to be retrievable from the other case. However, if one case is open the lid on its matching case will not open.

Name: Placeholder's Spacious Satchel
Description (Fluff): An otherwise normal-looking leather satchel with a series of golden runes woven around the mouth of the bag, its only purpose is to make travel and adventuring easier by holding as much as it can. The inside of the bag looks to be made completely of shadow, but in reality the bag's enchantment causes any item placed within it to be shrunken down to a tiny size and placed in magical stasis.
Effects: Any object can be stored in the bag, although it must fit within the mouth of the satchel - a little larger than most people's heads - and the bag can hold 100 cubic meters (the size of a modest closet) worth of stuff. The bag is always treated as an easily-accessible location. No items will fall out of the bag if it is upended, although there is a specific method that will cause the bag to empty out all items inside of it in a heap on the ground.

Name: Spirit Quest Ointment
Description (Fluff): A strange and useful concoction, this ointment is infused with a strong yet balanced degree of both positive and negative spiritual elements. Similar tinctures have been used by many cultures for meditations and spirit quests, and through the refinement of recipes used in many traditions this ointment is accepted among modern alchemists as the most powerful and effective version. Through a lengthy ritual application of the ointment, a person can examine and even repair deeper levels of their spirit, tending to their supernatural well-being as though a small garden or sculpture.
Effects: The ointment is applied painstakingly and the recipient must engage in a long meditation, the full process taking 24 hours which must be uninterrupted or the item is wasted without effect. If the process is completed, the user may completely reassign all of their Experience, then benefits from a full night’s rest.

Name: Light One-Handed Melee Weapon
Description (Fluff): A light, one-handed melee weapon — a dagger, hand axe, rapier, or similar; pick whatever fits your character.

Name: Heavy One-Handed Melee Weapon
Description (Fluff): A heavier one-handed melee weapon — a mace, shortsword, or similar; pick whatever fits your character.

Name: Light Two-Handed Melee Weapon
Description (Fluff): A light, two-handed melee weapon — a spear, quarterstaff, or similar; pick whatever fits your character.

Name: Heavy Two-Handed Melee Weapon
Description (Fluff): A heavy two-handed melee weapon — a greatsword, war hammer, or similar; pick whatever fits your character.

Name: Light Thrown Weapon
Description (Fluff): A light thrown weapon — throwing knives, darts, or similar.
Effects: Only has a Range of Close when used with Melee.

Name: Heavy Thrown Weapon
Description (Fluff): A heavy thrown weapon — a javelin, hand axe meant for throwing, or similar.
Effects: Only has a Range of Close when used with Melee.

Name: Light Bow
Description (Fluff): A light bow, requiring two hands to wield.

Name: Heavy Bow
Description (Fluff): A heavy bow, requiring two hands to wield.

Name: Unarmed
Description (Fluff): Fighting with fists, claws, or whatever's on hand — no weapon required, and doesn't occupy a Held slot.

Name: Shield
Description (Fluff): A shield, occupying one Held slot — used for its high Defense bonus rather than to deal damage.

Name: Light Armor
Description (Fluff): Light armor — a gambeson or jacket reinforced with small pieces of wood, or similar.

Name: Heavy Armor
Description (Fluff): Heavy armor — made from plate or heavy chains of metal, or similar.

Name: Blunderbuss
Description (Fluff): The standard Goblin firearm is a short-barreled musket that fires little bits of metal, essentially a shotgun with a flared muzzle.
Effects: Has Good Luck on attacks within 5 meters, and Bad Luck on attacks between 10 and 15 meters. Takes 1 AP to reload.

Name: Handgun
Description (Fluff): A small firearm meant to be held in a single hand, firing a slug or ball of metal.
Effects: Two Handguns can be used at once to briefly avoid reloading, which Goblins often use to let out a volley, stow them, and charge into melee. Takes 1 AP to reload.

Name: Musket
Description (Fluff): A firearm with a long, straight barrel that fires a slug or ball of metal, designed as best as Goblins can for accuracy — more of a specialist weapon that isn't used in large numbers in fights.
Effects: Takes 1 AP to reload.

Name: Bomb
Description (Fluff): The standard bomb, if anything Goblins make can have a standard, is a hollow rigid object filled with gunpowder. Most are very crudely made.
Effects: A Level 2 alchemical Grenade, requiring Fire material to craft. Deals its Damage to the target and any adjacent squares. Follows the [Grenade] rules when thrown — targets the foe's Dodge Defense, cannot Gamble on the attack, and is consumed after use. Bombs are prone to mishap: if a diamond is kept as the result of the Throwing flip to use one on a Card Value of 1, the wielder also takes 6 Physical damage.

Name: Rockbiter's Bomb
Description (Fluff): The Rockbiter tribe's sole technological improvement on the standard bomb has been using hollowed-out, stalactite-shaped crustacean shells as the container, which greatly improves its accuracy when thrown — and lets a particularly stupid or brave Goblin use it as a Light melee weapon that explodes on hit.
Effects: A Level 2 alchemical Grenade, requiring Fire material to craft. Deals its Damage to the target and any adjacent squares. Can be used as a Light melee weapon that explodes on hit. When thrown, follows the [Grenade] rules — targets the foe's Dodge Defense, cannot Gamble on the attack, and is consumed after use. Bombs are prone to mishap: if a diamond is kept as the result of the Throwing flip to use one on a Card Value of 1, the wielder also takes 6 Physical damage.

Name: Smoking Hills Bomb
Description (Fluff): Smoking Hills tribes have further improved the bomb's design, using the shells of metallic thermophile snails as the container. These well-made bombs do not have an accuracy penalty, but cannot be used effectively as a melee weapon.
Effects: A Level 2 alchemical Grenade, requiring Fire material to craft. Deals its Damage to the target and any adjacent squares. Follows the [Grenade] rules when thrown — targets the foe's Dodge Defense, cannot Gamble on the attack, and is consumed after use. Bombs are prone to mishap: if a diamond is kept as the result of the Throwing flip to use one on a Card Value of 1, the wielder also takes 6 Physical damage.

Name: Shroud of Shadowy Stillness
Description (Fluff): A thin, gossamer cape that looks almost woven out of shadows, valued by scoundrels engaging in illegal business and those who simply cherish peace and quiet alike.
Effects: While wearing the shroud and not moving, the wearer becomes very hard to perceive, and has Good Luck on Stealth flips as long as they remain still.

Name: Watcher's Mantle
Description (Fluff): A thick, fur mantle that provides the wearer with a sense of comfort and alertness.
Effects: The wearer does not tire and never needs to sleep, and may benefit from a full night's rest whenever they choose - they may still only benefit from such a rest once per 24 hours, as usual. This only functions once the wearer has worn the mantle continuously for a full day.

Name: Shawl of the Land
Description (Fluff): Woven from cloth, ivy, fur, and other natural materials, these shawls were originally created by druidic sects to help wearers become more attuned to, and draw sustenance from, the earth.
Effects: The wearer does not need to eat or drink, and is nourished as though they were eating regular meals. They heal an extra 1 Health from getting a full night's rest. These benefits only function once the wearer has worn the shawl continuously for 24 hours.

Name: Choker of Defiance
Description (Fluff): A simple, unadorned choker that thrums faintly with a defiant energy, resisting whatever fate seems to have in store.
Effects: This choker has [twice the enhancement's Level] charges, regained after a full night's rest. Before making a flip, the wearer may spend X charges to Sift X cards and add their suits to the suit pool.

Name: Cloak of Faces
Description (Fluff): An incredibly rare, and by some accounts distasteful, item - usually made of rough leather, heavy and large, with a spacious hood.
Effects: Placed over the face of a recently-deceased humanoid, after a full round the cloak steals the corpse's face, leaving only bone and muscle beneath. After wearing the cloak for a full day, the wearer becomes attuned to it (lasting until another wearer attunes instead) and is aware of every face it has ever stolen. For 2 AP, the wearer may raise the hood and replace their face with any face the cloak has stolen - this actually changes their features, not an illusion, until the hood is lowered.

Name: Field Surgeon's Handwraps
Description (Fluff): Thin gloves that appear to be wrapped from bandaging, carrying a subtle mint scent - any liquid or dirt that stains them fades away after only a short time.
Effects: The wearer has Good Luck on Medicine flips.

Name: Gloves of Spatial Distortion
Description (Fluff): Fine gloves of flexible leather, their cuffs stitched with a spiderweb of silver and gold threading.
Effects: For 3 AP, the wearer may designate two points on solid surfaces within 20 meters they can see - one an entrance, one an exit, each about half a meter wide. The wearer and anything they've touched that round may pass through the entrance and emerge from the exit, as though the two surfaces were joined by a window. Only the wearer can see the points (a faint shimmering distortion), though onlookers will notice an arm or object emerging from a solid surface. The points last for the encounter, or until the gloves create a new pair.

Name: Shadowcat Slippers
Description (Fluff): Dull, unassuming slippers of black cloth. The wearer finds they have a surprising grip, springing up walls as easily as cobblestone roads.
Effects: The wearer can run up walls and other vertical surfaces, but must end their turn on a stable surface or fall.

Name: Greaves of the Warlock King
Description (Fluff): Ornate greaves said to have been worn by a warlock-king who ruled through speed and surprise as much as sorcery.
Effects: Once per turn, for 1 AP, the wearer may Teleport [twice their Speed] meters.

Name: Ring of Charming, Assertive, or Bold Statements
Description (Fluff): Smithed from thick metals, usually simple in style - iron, or an extravagant blend of gold, platinum, and other precious metals. The wearer finds that when they make an earnest request, a convincing argument, or a menacing threat, their words carry extra weight.
Effects: This ring is created as a ring of Charming, Assertive, or Bold Statements, chosen when the item is created. Once per encounter, the wearer may gain Good Luck on a Statement made using Rapport (if Charming), Persuasion (if Assertive), or Presence (if Bold).

Name: Ring of Pure Elements
Description (Fluff): A large ring studded with a variety of multi-colored gemstones.
Effects: Once per encounter, when the wearer makes a damaging spell attack, they may have it deal its damage as Fire, Frost, Brilliant, or Shadow instead of its normal type.

Name: Heartseeker
Description (Fluff): Forged of a blood-red steel, or some equally sinister material, the bearer feels a subtle pressure guiding their strikes toward the heart of anyone who stands against them.
Effects: When the wielder makes an attack with this weapon, they may treat any card flipped for it as a Heart.

Name: Valiant Arms
Description (Fluff): Reinforced and sturdy, the style of this weapon makes it feel reassuring in one's hands.
Effects: When this weapon is used to make an attack, if the wielder moved at least 6 meters in a relatively straight line this turn, they have Good Luck on the attack.

Name: Placeholder's Speedy Scepter
Description (Fluff): The legendary regalia considered the pinnacle of Placeholder's illustrious enchanting career, serving as a near-perfect conduit for magical power.
Effects: Abilities used with this cost 1 less AP, to a minimum of 1 AP.

Name: Immaculate Spice Rack
Description (Fluff): A set of crystalline vials and bottles secured in a soft leather case, haunted by a variety of salacious aromas, each etched with runes detailing the essence contained within.
Effects: When used to create or season a culinary dish, the user has Good Luck on any related flips.

Name: Unmovable Bar
Description (Fluff): A round iron bar with small grooves at either end and no other discernible features, save for faint runes along its surface.
Effects: When the grooves are rotated in a specific manner, the bar hangs in place and does not move from where it is - even if staying in place defies gravity - until the grooves are rotated back. An unmovable bar can support up to 1,000 kilograms before falling, and requires the same amount of force to move.

Name: Placeholder's Indelible Instrument
Description (Fluff): A small metal pen, unadorned outside but filled with a fine mesh of crystal and lenses. Its tip is smooth, black stone.
Effects: When drawn across a surface, the pen leaves a black mark. The mark doesn't change the surface, only colors it, and can only be removed by damaging the item - scraping away the surface, carving away wood, and so on. A mark on a living creature fades once the creature sheds its skin.

Name: Placeholder's Wondrous Workspace
Description (Fluff): This large chest counts as any set of tools needed to create items, including a forge.
Effects: The chest fulfills the tool or Skill Kit requirement for any creation School.

Name: Cart, Medium
Description (Fluff): A more substantial wooden cart, reinforced with metal and generally large enough that it requires a handful of people or a pack animal to pull along.
Effects: Enough room for a few humanoids, several moderately-sized crates of trade goods, or a similar load.

Name: Wagon, Large
Description (Fluff): A great wooden wagon, made from sturdy timber and bands of iron. Wagons of this size generally have walls and a covered top, with a bench for the driver and a cabin for passengers and cargo - designs vary between cultures, from loading ramps for cargo wagons to fold-down stage walls for traveling performers.
Effects: Enough room for several people and their belongings, or a couple dozen barrels or crates of goods, assuming the interior isn't used for other features.

Name: Cap of Smug Confidence
Description (Fluff): These hats are simple but impressively crafted, designed in an understated fashion but woven with silver threading and other expensive materials.
Effects: The wearer has their anxieties dampened, and gains a +1 bonus to Instinct Defense against Statements.

Name: Stoic Skullcap
Description (Fluff): These caps provide the wearer a sense of calm and clarity when dealing with others, a feeling that intensifies the more another tries to menace or win them over with raw charisma.
Effects: The wearer gains a +1 bonus to Mental Defense against Statements.

Name: Sympathetic Hat
Description (Fluff): The enchantment placed on these hats helps attune the emotions of the wearer with those around them - not enough to affect their own thoughts or desires, but enough to help them understand the feelings that drive others.
Effects: The wearer gains a +1 bonus to Instinct Defense.

Name: Wizardly Hat of Tam the Tipsy
Description (Fluff): An old, battered wizard's hat with a wide brim and a long, pointy tip, patched and stained many times. Its haggard appearance is part of its power - the hat contains the power of the famous sorcerer-brewmaster Tam the Tipsy.
Effects: Whenever the wearer drinks Alcohol, they may regain the use of an Encounter Technique with a Level equal to or lower than the Alcohol's own Level.

Name: Headband of Telepathy
Description (Fluff): A headband, bandanna, or full hat with a band inside, woven with silver threads and clear crystals typically used in divination magics.
Effects: The wearer can communicate telepathically with one creature they can see within 20 meters, for the rest of the scene.

Name: Cloak of One Thousand Feathers
Description (Fluff): A breathtaking number of soft, smooth feathers stitched into a wispy cloak that billows and flows slightly, even in still air.
Effects: Whenever the wearer would fall, instead they glide - moving 5 meters toward the ground and 5 meters horizontally, as they choose - ignoring any effects of falling from a height regardless of distance. This takes no action to do, but while gliding the wearer cannot move normally.

Name: Cape of Many Pockets
Description (Fluff): Usually large and dramatic, in the style of warm, bulky traveler's cloaks, these capes feature a dozen pouches along the outside or inside, barely large enough to fit a hand in but capable of holding objects much larger.
Effects: The cape has 12 pouches, each an easily-accessible container that can hold an object no larger than 1 meter in any dimension. Stored items are weightless and cannot be damaged; if the cape is destroyed, everything stored in it tumbles out unharmed.

Name: Jerkin of the Land
Description (Fluff): Armor created in a simple style, usually incorporating cloth, ivy, fur, and other natural materials - made by druidic sects to help its wearer become more attuned to, and draw sustenance from, the earth.
Effects: The wearer does not need to eat or drink, and is nourished as though they were eating regular meals. They heal an extra 1 Health from getting a full night's rest.

Name: Fitted Armor
Description (Fluff): Heavier armor provides protection at the cost of mobility, but some talented smiths can mitigate this limitation - by connecting the plate and chain of heavy armor in specific ways, the craftsman creates armor that limits the wearer's movement less than it otherwise would.
Effects: The armor's Might Requirement is reduced by 1.

Name: Sorcerer's Gloves
Description (Fluff): Light, silken gloves woven with silver and gold thread, extremely durable despite seeming thin and fragile. When the wearer channels magical energy, gemstones stitched along the gloves light up in a variety of colors.
Effects: The wearer can throw a bolt of energy at a creature within their Sorcery Skill Total in meters, making a Sorcery attack against the target's Dodge or Parry Defense. On a hit, it deals 3 + [Mind] Physical damage.

Name: Apprentice's Dueling Catalyst
Description (Fluff): Traditionally crafted as a staff, although sometimes found as ritual daggers or scepters, these foci control the energy channeled through them to ensure the wielder's magic doesn't kill their target.
Effects: Spell attacks made using this as an Implement that would Down a creature instead render them unconscious rather than killing them.

Name: Staying Gauntlets
Description (Fluff): Simple gauntlets, treated with a numbing salve worked into the leather. A fighter wearing them finds their blows land softer than they mean them to - never quite enough to land a killing stroke, only enough to take the fight out of someone.
Effects: Weapon attacks made by the wearer that would Down a creature instead render them unconscious rather than killing them.

Name: Elemental Bloodletter
Description (Fluff): Often etched with runes of power or augmented to be more magically conductive, these weapons convert part of each attack into the enchantment's corresponding element - a flaming sword might have gouts of flame leap off the blade with each strike, a shadowed axe might have its blade wreathed in darkness.
Effects: When the weapon is created, choose Fire, Frost, Brilliant, or Shadow - it deals its damage as that type instead of Physical. Whenever an attack with it would cause a creature to lose Health, they instead gain that many stacks of Bleeding.

Name: Sanguine Iron Weapon
Description (Fluff): These weapons' properties are due largely to the process by which they're constructed - gathering large amounts of blood and magically sifting the iron from it, then working it into a blade with an incredibly strong sympathy for the blood of living creatures.
Effects: Whenever an attack with the weapon causes the target to lose Health, they also gain a stack of Bleeding.

Name: Returning Knives
Description (Fluff): While this enchantment is commonly placed on knives or other small missiles, it can in theory be worked into any weapon designed to be thrown.
Effects: When the weapon is thrown as part of an attack, at the start of the wielder's next turn it returns to their hand.

Name: Spiritlink Scepter
Description (Fluff): Traditionally crafted as a wooden scepter, although occasionally done in other styles or even as other weapons. Much of the weapon is wrapped in scraps of prayer shawl and adorned with simple beads, and while held the wielder feels a faint, insubstantial energy flow through them, like a flowing river or a spring breeze.
Effects: Theurgy spells cast using this as an Implement have their Range increased by 3 meters. For such spells that aren't ranged, the wielder may choose any point within 3 meters of themself to be their location for determining the spell's targets or area of effect.

Name: Scepter of Evocation
Description (Fluff): A focus surging with elemental power, which the wielder can tap into with some effort.
Effects: A spell cast using this as an Implement that would normally cost 2 or fewer AP may instead be cast for 4 AP. If it is, the caster has Good Luck on any attacks made as part of the spell.

Name: Quartermaster's Blade
Description (Fluff): These weapons can be crafted in just about any style or appearance, from a worn and simple club to an elegant courtier's blade with precious metals worked in - fitting, since the weapon's enchantment lets it change its shape to that of any other weapon while keeping its own design and aesthetic.
Effects: As a Move, the wielder can change the weapon's shape to that of any other single weapon, including shields. If it's turned into a ranged weapon, it does not create ammunition.

Name: Windrider's Loop
Description (Fluff): A winding ring of steel and silver, wrapping a dozen times around the wearer's finger. When worn, the wearer feels the breeze more strongly against their hand.
Effects: Once per encounter, when making a weapon attack, the wearer may increase that weapon's Range by 5 meters.

Name: Surestride Boots
Description (Fluff): These boots come in a variety of designs, from hiking boots to snowshoes, but the enchantment powering them stays the same - desired by trappers, explorers, and anyone who spends time in the wilderness, giving their wearer a firm foothold on almost any landscape.
Effects: The wearer ignores 2 levels of Difficult Terrain.

Name: Placeholder's Bottomless Belt
Description (Fluff): Crafted in an unassuming style - only close inspection reveals the belt's secrets. Careful application of spatial enchantments gives this belt multiple compartments transposed over each other, letting the wearer store an entire alchemist's workshop in a single belt.
Effects: The belt has 20 pouches, each an easily-accessible container that can hold a small object such as a Potion or Grenade.

Name: Basic Conveniences
Description (Fluff): Covers a wide variety of goods that don't require any particular knowledge to make - soap, reduced dyes, filtered lubricants and oils, wax and other materials for treating wood and leather, polished stone, and so on.
Effects: Except for specific recipes, this category likely covers whatever a character wants to make with basic alchemical skill.

Name: Charcoal
Description (Fluff): Charcoal from a woodfire, filtered and purified with some special preparation, kept in small pieces in a pouch or other container.
Effects: If a creature ingests a Poison, fails their Resistance flip to avoid its effect, and eats a mouthful of charcoal within 1 minute, they may immediately make another Resistance flip against it, with Good Luck.

Name: Incense, Simple
Description (Fluff): Used widely across many cultures for ritual and everyday use, simple incense has an indistinct, muddled aroma - not the quality one would use for a serious ritual, but common in cheap taverns, brothels, and fortune-tellers' parlors. Sold in bricks that burn for a few hours.

Name: Incense, Quality
Description (Fluff): Made by a skilled alchemist from more particular ingredients, quality incense is distinctly better than simply burning plants in a jar.

Name: Oil
Description (Fluff): A basic good burned in lamps and used for a variety of other things, sold in a small flask. Rendering it pure enough to burn properly takes some basic alchemical skill, though not much.

Name: Alcohol, Simple
Description (Fluff): Among the most basic and relatively weak alcohols one can make - ale from a low-end tavern, wine from a large stone jug, "whiskey" from the most questionable of grains.
Effects: One "drink" is about a pint or half-liter.

Name: Alcohol, Decent
Description (Fluff): Made by someone who actually knows what they're doing - a solid beer, a wine with an actual vintage, a hard liquor that's genuinely enjoyable.
Effects: One "drink" is about a pint or half-liter.

Name: Alcohol, Quality
Description (Fluff): A step above common taproom swill - the kind of drink with an actual name behind it, distilled or brewed by someone with real skill.
Effects: One "drink" is about a pint or half-liter.

Name: Alcohol, Artisanal
Description (Fluff): Crafted by a renowned distiller or vintner, the kind of bottle worth remembering the name of.
Effects: One "drink" is about a pint or half-liter.

Name: Alcohol, Legendary
Description (Fluff): Transcends mere technique - a bottle of spirits that only results from a substantial undertaking, the kind used to curry favor from kings and archmages.
Effects: One "drink" is about a pint or half-liter.

Name: Embalming Fluid
Description (Fluff): Used across cultures to preserve the dead - mummification rites, or more academic and occult practices like preserving organs in jars.
Effects: Any organic matter fully covered in embalming fluid does not decay. For a full corpse, this usually means soaking and wrapping it in bandages rather than submerging it. Embalming fluid is harmful if ingested, behaving as a dangerous Poison.

Name: Quicktorch
Description (Fluff): A wooden stick with a specially prepared head, hollowed out and treated with alchemical mixtures that react violently when struck against a rough surface.
Effects: Functions as a normal torch, except it may be lit for 1 AP without needing any other tools.

Name: Recreational Drugs, Poor Quality
Description (Fluff): Naturally-occurring plants smoked or ingested for a high exist alongside manufactured drugs - for drugs of this quality, the refining process was done improperly, the base materials were too poor, or the drug itself is simply dangerous. These form strong habits, and withdrawal can be lethal.

Name: Recreational Drugs, Quality
